title: Is there a quicker way to multiply ninety seven by twenty five?
description: Ninety seven is written as one hundred minus three, so the product becomes one hundred lots of twenty five take away three lots of twenty five. Both lots are easy numbers to find. Keeko doubts that only one three is taken away.
teaching_notes: One idea: write a number just below a round number as a difference in a bracket, then multiply each term. Watch for students who forget to multiply the three by twenty five.

video_script.why: A learner sees a quicker way to multiply a number just below a hundred, by using a difference in a bracket.
video_script.substitution: Replace ninety seven and twenty five with any number just below a round number and any multiplier.
video_script.anchor: one hundred lots of twenty five with three lots of twenty five taken away
video_script.wrong_answer: ninety seven times twenty five is one hundred times twenty five minus three
video_script.wrong_move: takes away only 3 instead of 3 lots of 25, so the 25 does not reach the 3
video_script.payoff_line: Ninety seven times twenty five is two thousand four hundred and twenty five.

final_answer.spoken: ninety seven times twenty five is two thousand four hundred and twenty five

video_script.design: A block of one hundred lots of twenty five with a small block of three lots of twenty five cut away from it.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; 97 × 25 written large with a question mark beside it

marks.h3: a number line marks 97 just before 100
marks.h4: a question mark glows over the product

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about a quicker way to multiply.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>We want ninety seven times twenty five.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>Ninety seven is very close to a round number.
<bookmark mark='h4'/>Which round number is it, and how can that help us?

beats.on_screen: the product and the number line stay on the board and the question mark keeps glowing

marks.t1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a block of 100 lots of 25 with 3 lots of 25 cut away, leaving 97 lots

marks.g1: the block of one hundred lots of twenty five is drawn
marks.g2: three lots are cut away from the end
marks.g3: the block that is left is marked as ninety seven lots

beats.colours: the three cut lots in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Ninety seven is three less than one hundred.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Ninety seven lots of a number are one hundred lots with three lots taken away.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>A difference in a bracket can stand for ninety seven.
<bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, ninety seven times twenty five.
<bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to find the product by writing ninety seven as one hundred minus three.

marks.s11: 97 splits into 100 and 3 with a minus sign
marks.s12: the difference goes inside a bracket with 25 outside

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, write ninety seven as one hundred minus three, because it is three less than a hundred.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>The product is open bracket one hundred minus three close bracket times twenty five.

marks.s21: the 25 is copied after 100 and after 3
marks.s22: the bracket is removed and the minus sign stays

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, remove the bracket, because the twenty five multiplies each term inside it.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>This gives one hundred times twenty five minus three times twenty five.
<bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, find each part.
One hundred times twenty five is two thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>Three times twenty five is seventy five, so we take seventy five from two thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>Ninety seven times twenty five is two thousand four hundred and twenty five.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='k1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 100 × 25 − 3; it is struck out and 100 × 25 − 3 × 25 takes its place
narration: <bookmark mark='k2'/>Keeko thinks ninety seven times twenty five is one hundred times twenty five minus three.
<bookmark mark='k3'/>But the three is multiplied by twenty five as well.
<bookmark mark='k4'/>Every part of the bracket gets multiplied.
